12h-t.name: Toyota 12H-T
12h-t.notes: Turbocharged 2H, gear-driven timing, direct injection. Mechanical injection pump, no ECU - predates Toyota's electronically-controlled diesels.

13b-t.name: Toyota 13B-T
13b-t.notes: Originally a Dyna/Coaster truck engine, not a factory Land Cruiser fitment — a well-documented swap into 4-cylinder-bay 70-series chassis. Mechanical injection pump (no E suffix), no ECU.

1fz-fe.name: Toyota 1FZ-FE
1fz-fe.notes: Electronic fuel injection with its own ECU.

1hd-fte.name: Toyota 1HD-FTE (non-intercooled)
1hd-fte.notes: This is the non-intercooled 70-series tune of the 1HD-FTE - the 100-series version of the same engine code is intercooled and rated higher, but that chassis generation is out of scope here. Electronically controlled injection (ECU), unlike the earlier mechanical 1HD-T.

1hd-t.name: Toyota 1HD-T
1hd-t.notes: Inline-6 — will not fit 4-cylinder-only bays like the lj78's without major surgery (see fitment overrides). Mechanical injection pump, no ECU (later 1HD-FTE moved to electronic control).

1hz.name: Toyota 1HZ
1hz.notes: Mechanical injection pump, no ECU - one of the simpler engines to run standalone in a swap.

1kd-ftv.name: Toyota 1KD-FTV
1kd-ftv.notes: Modern common-rail D-4D diesel (Prado/Hilux/Fortuner-family, 2000-2015). Output varies significantly by market/year/emissions tune (roughly 134-188hp, 300-420Nm across variants) - 170hp/410Nm used here as a representative mid-range figure. Popular swap into older Land Cruisers for its reliability and torque, but its bellhousing pattern doesn't match the older 1HZ/1HD-T family - dedicated adapter/conversion kits exist for exactly this reason. Not factory-fitted to any of our seeded frames.

1kz-t.name: Toyota 1KZ-T
1kz-t.notes: Mechanical-injection (non-EFI) version of the 1KZ-TE, used in lighter-duty export/general-market Prado variants. Simpler to run standalone in a swap than the electronic 1KZ-TE.

1kz-te.name: Toyota 1KZ-TE
1kz-te.notes: Factory engine in successor Prado 90-series (KZJ) chassis sharing this body/bay family — treated as a bolt-in for lj78 (see fitment overrides), not stock there. Electronic injection pump - a failed real-world LJ78 swap (see cataloged build) traced directly to running it off the older 2L-TE's ECU instead of its own.

1pz.name: Toyota 1PZ
1pz.notes: Toyota's unusual 5-cylinder diesel, naturally aspirated, mechanical injection pump. A distinct bellhousing pattern from the I4/I6 diesel families.

22r.name: Toyota 22R
22r.notes: Carbureted, shared with contemporary Hilux/4Runner. No ECU.

2b.name: Toyota 2B
2b.notes: Bored-out successor to the B, naturally aspirated, mechanical injection pump.

2h.name: Toyota 2H
2h.notes: Bored/stroked successor to the H, naturally aspirated, mechanical injection pump. Predecessor to 1HZ.

2l-te.name: Toyota 2L-TE
2l-te.notes: The 'TE' suffix denotes Toyota's electronically-controlled injection pump generation - needs the donor ECU/harness, not just mechanical fuel/throttle linkages.

3b.name: Toyota 3B
3b.notes: The most widely-used classic B-family diesel across late 40/60/70-series - naturally aspirated, mechanical injection pump. hp/torque cited varies somewhat by year/injection-pump revision (roughly 90-98hp across sources); 90hp/217Nm used here as a representative baseline.

3f.name: Toyota 3F
3f.notes: Carbureted successor to the 2F, no ECU. FJ61 straddles the 3F/3F-E era - treated here as 3F pending clearer per-unit confirmation.

3f-e.name: Toyota 3F-E
3f-e.notes: Fuel-injected version of the 3F, with its own ECU - fitted to the JDM 'VX' grade FJ62G to let it be sold as a passenger-class vehicle in Japan.

3l.name: Toyota 3L
3l.notes: Naturally-aspirated, non-turbo diesel - a cheaper alternative to the 2L-T/2L-TE used in most other LJ-series Prados. Mechanical injection pump.

b.name: Toyota B
b.notes: Toyota's original 40-series diesel; naturally aspirated, mechanical injection pump. Superseded by 2B, then 3B.

bmw-m52.name: BMW M52B28
bmw-m52.notes: A common swap into Central American LJ70-family chassis, often paired with the factory BMW 5-speed. Electronic fuel injection with its own ECU/DME.

bmw-m57.name: BMW M57D30 (530d)
bmw-m57.notes: A verified real-world swap into an LJ78 used a 2003 E39 530d donor (see cataloged build). Distinct from the gas M52B28 already seeded - shares BMW's period bellhousing family but is a turbodiesel, not gas. Common-rail with its own ECU/DDE - that real build kept the donor's intact harness/ECU/pedal for exactly this reason.

cummins-r28.name: Cummins R2.8
cummins-r28.notes: Crate diesel marketed specifically for 4x4 repower/swap use; torque is factory-limited on the stock ECU tune to protect period-correct drivelines. Modern common-rail with its own ECU.

h.name: Toyota H
h.notes: Toyota's original inline-6 diesel, predecessor to 2H/12H-T/1HZ/1HD-T. Naturally aspirated, mechanical injection pump.

ls3.name: GM LS3
ls3.notes: Popular V8 swap-in across many off-road platforms; wide but relatively short/light for its output. Drive-by-wire ECU - needs the donor harness/ECU (or a standalone controller) and often a DBW-to-DBC conversion for older platforms.
